# opv

> opv is a Rust CLI that syncs secrets from 1Password into runtime targets (Fly.io today; Azure, AWS and GCP planned) without ever printing, logging or writing a secret value. A committed `secrets.toml` declares IDs, key names, kinds and validation rules; values stay in 1Password.

Assistants setting opv up for a user: read the agent setup guide first and follow its rules. Never ask the user for a secret value, never read one (`op item get --reveal`, `op read`), and ask before `opv item skeleton`, `opv sync`, `--deploy`, `--prune`, `--rotate` or `--prune-immutable`.

## Docs

- [Agent setup guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/agent-setup.md): step-by-step setup for AI assistants, with safety rules and exit codes
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/README.md): what opv is, quickstart, minimal configuration
- [Installing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/install.md): install script, binaries, npm, source, checksum verification, prerequisites
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/configuration.md): store layout, `secrets.toml`, simple and fleet profiles, `opv init`, rules and failure reasons
- [Usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/usage.md): commands, JSON output, change detection, pruning, exit codes, security model, GitHub Actions
